clue.text: Lease, for four seasons, a supplier to the dairy

blocks.note: four seasons make a year: A YR'S, with YR the usual abbreviation for year
to lease something is to hire it

explanation.surface: Someone renting out land for a year to a dairy supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first half as A YEAR'S HIRE: a lease that lasts four seasons.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ayrshire is a Scottish breed of dairy cattle, so the animal literally supplies milk to the dairy.

clue.text: Back to reality too soon, pa

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only its tail is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of reality
arriving too soon is arriving early

explanation.surface: A child complaining that Dad has come back to the real world too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pa' looks like a father, but it is the Latin abbreviation per annum.
explanation.definitionFit: Per annum, abbreviated p.a., means each year, which is what yearly describes.

clue.text: Younger men touring a modern marketplace picking up sauce ingredients

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards
to tour a place is to go all round it, so one set of letters surrounds the other

blocks.note: sons are the younger men of a family
taken as written
eBay is an online marketplace

explanation.surface: Young men browsing an online market for things to put in a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya beans are fermented to make soy sauce, so they are its basic ingredients.

clue.text: Indeed, and then some doubts expressed about the legal system?

definitions.text: doubts expressed about the legal system?

blocks.note: first meaning: an emphatic agreement, 'and how!'

blocks.clueFragment: doubts expressed about the legal system?
blocks.note: second meaning: read literally, a question asking whether the system is fair

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: someone asking whether the justice system is really just.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an emphatic yes, while its literal words question whether something is fair, the doubt a sceptic of the courts would voice.

clue.text: This person's delivered from mic when speaking

definitions.text: This person's delivered from mic when speaking

indicators.note: taken from the word, here its two outside letters
spoken out loud, the letters become the way they are said rather than written

blocks.note: the first and last letters of mic, said as letter names and written out in full

explanation.surface: A description of a host speaking into a microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: M and C said out loud give the spelt-out form of MC, master of ceremonies, and an MC is exactly someone who talks into a mic.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies or compère, the host who addresses the audience through a microphone.

clue.text: Expert leaves plant in East London?

blocks.note: a pro is an expert
tea leaves

explanation.surface: A specialist departing from a garden in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East London' suggests the Cockney East End; it is the city in South Africa, where the protea is the national flower. 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The protea is a flowering shrub native to South Africa, home of the city of East London.

clue.text: The best start

blocks.note: first meaning: the choicest
second meaning: to begin

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it sounds like praise for a good beginning; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for the choicest one and a verb for provoking or beginning a quarrel.

clue.text: This picnic could be better

blocks.note: first meaning, split in two
second meaning: to surpass someone

explanation.walkthrough: A DO is a party, so an outdoor party is an OUT DO.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo a rival is to surpass them, and a picnic is a social gathering held in the open air.

clue.text: Unrestrained voice, little being large

indicators.note: with nothing holding it in, the letters at each end are stripped away

blocks.note: a tenor is a singing voice
a mouse is a tiny creature

explanation.surface: A small creature with a loud, uninhibited voice that turns out to be big.
explanation.walkthrough: Join TENOR and MOUSE, then drop the outside letters of the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means very big, a stronger synonym of large.

clue.text: Little soul from old Egyptian times

blocks.note: in ancient Egyptian belief the ba was a part of the soul
as in multiplication: three by four

explanation.surface: A tiny spirit dating back to the age of the pharaohs.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective baby means small, as in baby carrots or baby grand.

clue.text: East End rogue put textile mill heist into action?

definitions.text: put textile mill heist into action?

blocks.note: first meaning: the villain of the soap EastEnders

blocks.clueFragment: put textile mill heist into action?
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: to steal fabric

explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in East London; NICK is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Cotton was the soap's notorious bad lot, and the name read as a phrase means stealing cotton from a mill.

clue.text: One ball ideally struck, eclipsing another missing the whole court

indicators.note: something struck is knocked about, so these letters are thrown into a new order
a word that is missing something has had part of it taken out
an eclipsing body passes in front and covers another, so one set of letters surrounds the next

blocks.note: a single ball is round, the shape of the letter O
taken as written, to be rearranged
another ball
the whole of something is all of it

explanation.surface: A cricket shot sweetly timed, with one ball hiding another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One ball' is a letter shaped like a ball, not a delivery; 'the whole' is the word to remove from another ball, leaving a single letter to tuck inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Bailey is the popular name for the Central Criminal Court in London.

clue.text: A visual sign medium is entranced?

indicators.note: someone entranced has been put into a deep state and is inside it

blocks.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
a coma is a deep trance-like state, which surrounds the letter for medium

explanation.surface: Asking whether a spiritualist in a trance is showing a sign you can see.
explanation.walkthrough: The medium looks like a psychic, but it is just the size letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma is a punctuation mark, a sign read by eye that marks a pause.

clue.text: A bar set high when entering sports event across country

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so these letters sit within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a perch is a raised bar for a bird
as means when
PE is physical education, school sports

explanation.surface: A high-jump bar being raised during a cross-country athletics meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports event' looks like one unit; 'sports' alone gives the outer letters and 'event across country' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper chase is a cross-country race in which runners follow a trail of scattered paper.

clue.text: Vessel switching government flag to port?

indicators.note: switching direction and heading to port, leftwards, means the letters run right to left

blocks.note: the Raj was British rule in India
to flag is to tire or sag

explanation.surface: A ship changing its ensign as it comes into harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the left side of a ship, so heading to port means going right to left. 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning droop.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas jar is a glass laboratory container for collecting gases.

clue.text: Tease wife

blocks.note: first meaning: to mock gently
second meaning: a humorous term for a wife

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to tease one's wife; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbing someone is mocking them, and Genesis has Eve fashioned from Adam's rib, hence the jocular term for a spouse.

clue.text: We're going to receive them from our friends at the Elysee Palace

definitions.text: We're going to receive them from our friends at the Elysee Palace

blocks.note: surface reading: gifts or guests coming our way

blocks.clueFragment: from our friends at the Elysee Palace
blocks.note: setter's reading: when we leave, the French say goodbye to us

explanation.walkthrough: 'We're going' is about leaving, not about future events, and the Elysée Palace stands for France.
explanation.definitionFit: The French plural word for farewells is what departing guests hear from French hosts.

clue.text: Provocative, one's put on vulgar finery

indicators.note: something vulgar is crude and coarse, so these letters are roughed up into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an ace is a one in cards; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone wearing gaudy clothes to provoke a reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: In-yer-face is slang for aggressively confrontational, deliberately designed to provoke.

clue.text: Fitting phase in play at the start, lycanthropes lying low

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept
the letters go inside the other word

blocks.note: play is fun
the first letters of both words
to low is to moo like cattle

explanation.surface: Werewolves hiding during a stage of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying low' looks like hiding, but low is the cattle noise. A full moon is fitting because lunacy and werewolf fits were blamed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The full moon is the lunar phase traditionally blamed for fits of madness and werewolf transformations.

clue.text: Uneasy, we go to get surgeons?

definitions.note: seen from the nurses' own side: we who work with surgeons

indicators.note: uneasy letters are unsettled and so shift into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to take away

explanation.surface: Nervous staff leaving to fetch the surgeons.
explanation.walkthrough: This works in reverse: the answer plus GO, shuffled, makes SURGEONS, so speaking as the answer, 'we' add 'go' to get surgeons.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is spoken in the voice of hospital nurses, the staff who assist surgeons, so 'we' stands for them.

clue.text: Extras later!

blocks.note: first meaning: two byes, runs scored as extras in cricket
second meaning: a casual farewell, see you later

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter untouched, and counts among the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye-bye is an informal goodbye, the same parting as 'later!', and also two cricket byes side by side.

clue.text: Flat race pro knocked off after climbing a mountain

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading from the bottom upwards
something knocked off is removed from the word

blocks.note: AN ALP, an Alpine peak
taken as written
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A professional flat-race jockey thrown off after riding up a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat race' reads as horse racing, but 'Flat' is the definition and 'race' a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: Planar means lying in a single plane, so a planar surface is flat.

clue.text: Form you poetically may frame in reflective mode?

definitions.text: Form you poetically may frame in reflective mode?

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so these letters surround the other word
a reflection in a mirror reverses, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: ye is the archaic and poetic form of you
to gel is to take form

explanation.surface: Advice to a poet on what shape a contemplative verse might take.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a poetic form of mournful reflection, which is exactly what you might compose in a reflective mood.

clue.text: Bother, one's discovered in crossword pattern

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the cover off, so the outside letters go and the middle stays
the letter goes inside the other word

blocks.note: the grid is the pattern of squares
the middle of one; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Annoyance that someone has been found hiding in a crossword grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' reads as found, but means uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: A grind is a tiresome chore, something that is a bother to get through.

clue.text: Song intoned by Norman Stanley Fletcher?

indicators.note: something intoned is spoken out loud, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: Norman Stanley Fletcher of the sitcom Porridge was played by Ronnie Barker

explanation.surface: A question about what a famous TV jailbird might sing.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge was a British TV sitcom set in a prison; its lead, Fletcher, was Ronnie Barker's best-known part.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a song of the Venetian gondoliers, or music written in that rocking style.

clue.text: Make distribution of shares, Genesis to Malachi inclusive

blocks.note: including everything, all of it
the first and last books of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A financial instruction framed as reading the Bible from cover to cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot shares is to distribute them among applicants, the usual term for a share issue.

clue.text: Goodness goes on for ever

blocks.note: as in 'the saying goes', where goes stands for is
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Kindness that lasts without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness' looks like virtue, but it is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: I say! is a dated British exclamation of surprise, just like crying goodness!

clue.text: Some music fans cool it after contretemps

indicators.note: a contretemps is a mishap or squabble, after which things are in disarray

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Music lovers calming down after a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic sol-fa is a system of naming notes (doh, ray, me) used to teach singing, so it is a form of music.

clue.text: Out for love, this relative would be a source of joy for sailor

indicators.note: the source is where a word begins, its first letter
the answer is what the outing would be without that letter

blocks.note: a jaunt is a trip out for pleasure
the first letter of joy
surface padding, an extra joke: with a Y added the trip becomes naval slang for a master-at-arms

explanation.surface: An aunt who would delight a sailor if she were out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: The trip minus that letter gives the answer; add a Y to the trip and you have JAUNTY, naval slang for a master-at-arms, hence the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family relative.

clue.text: Sometime during June 7, 1944?

blocks.note: on, as in on Monday, means during
D-Day was June 6, 1944, so the next day is E-Day

explanation.surface: A question about events in the days after the Normandy landings.
explanation.definitionFit: One day means at some unspecified time, just as sometime does.

clue.text: Brit's means to reach Sorbonne after solving Fermat's Last Theorem?

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, the only one kept
solving a problem works it out, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the final letter of Fermat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mathematician heading to a Paris university after cracking a famous problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sorbonne is in Paris, and a Briton would get there on the city's underground railway, the Métro.
